query: A Familiar Grin Before the next bout someone vaults the rope into the chalk: Corvin, sleeves rolled, wand spinning. He sees you and his grin slips. "Saint. Of course it's you." Then, low: "I owe three people money, and one of them has started describing what happens next. The house pays double for a grudge match. So hate me. Loudly." Fight him for real You knock his wand into the crowd on the fifth exchange. "Rude," he says from the flagstones, and laughs, but his eyes go to the bookmaker's slate and stay there a moment too long. He was never where your spell landed. He hauls you up by the collar, collects his purse, and presses a few coins of it into your hand. "Your cut, for the hating. You were very convincing." Put on a show, and let him win You shout, he shouts, sparks fly everywhere but at each other, and you go down with a groan the back row will talk about all week. The bettors who backed you never know. Corvin does. "I owe you," he says on the steps. "Add it to the list."
